newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA home-care referrals probed - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA home-care referrals probed - WSJ.

text.p: A federal probe into Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp's operations in El Paso, Texas focused on physician referrals to the company's home health-care agencies, the Wall Street Journal said Tuesday.

Federal investigators are also interested in Columbia/HCA's home health-care operations in other states, the newspaper said in its electronic edition, citing a government official with knowledge of the probe.
On March 19, the company said its El Paso operations were served with search warrants in connection with a federal investigation.
It was not immediately available to comment on the report.
A Columbia spokeswoman was quoted in the paper as saying she did not "see any value in speculating" about the nature of the investigation.

Columbia/HCA's homecare unit aimed to bring in $188 million this year in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, the paper said citing internal company documents it had obtained.

The newspaper said a lawsuit filed against the company last spring in El Paso alleged Columbia/HCA "created collusive business agreements and other arrangements with staff physicians...whereby staff physicians have profit incentive to influence and direct patient referrals," in order to boost its home-care division.
The company called the suit "groundless," the paper said.
